title: Heating Processes: Specific Heat and Latent Heat
seo_title: Year 11 Physics: Heating Processes Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Temperature, heat and internal energy; thermal equilibrium; heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation; specific heat capacity and latent heat; the first law of thermodynamics. (Senior Secondary Physics, Unit 1: Thermal, nuclear and electrical physics)
meta_desc: Free Year 11 Physics worksheets on heating processes: temperature, internal energy, conduction, convection, radiation, Q = mcΔT, latent heat and the first law of thermodynamics. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Q = mcΔT changes temperature; Q = mL changes state.
key_sub: Heat flows from hot to cold until thermal equilibrium.
body_html:
How to think about it

Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles; internal energy is their total kinetic and potential energy; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Energy moves by conduction, convection and radiation.

To change temperature: Q = mcΔT. To change state at constant temperature: Q = mL (L is the specific latent heat). The first law of thermodynamics is conservation of energy: ΔU = Q − W.

Example

Heat needed to warm 2.0 kg of water by 15 K (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹)?

Q = 2.0 × 4180 × 15

Answer: 1.25 × 10⁵ J

Example

Energy to melt 0.50 kg of ice (L = 3.34 × 10⁵ J/kg)?

Q = mL = 0.50 × 3.34 × 10⁵

Answer: 1.67 × 10⁵ J

Common mistakes

  • Using Q = mcΔT during a change of state.
  • Saying cold flows into an object: heat flows out of it.
  • Forgetting to convert grams to kilograms.

faq.q: Why does the temperature stay the same while water boils?
faq.a: The energy supplied is used to separate the particles (increase their potential energy), not to speed them up, so the temperature stays at 100 °C.

faq.q: Why is water good for storing heat?
faq.a: It has a high specific heat capacity (4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹), so it takes in a lot of energy for a small temperature rise.
